title: Cross-tenant correlated anomaly fusion and alert deduplication pipeline
creator: Ava Kim
description:
Problem: Our console notifies SREs and customers about usage/cost/latency anomalies independently per-tenant and per-signal. This yields noisy, duplicated alerts when a single underlying incident causes correlated shifts across metrics (e.g., a regional outage creating latency spikes + increased retry costs across multiple customers). The noise reduces signal-to-noise for oncall teams and increases mean time to resolution for true incidents.

Goal: Build a backend pipeline that fuses related anomaly signals across tenants, metrics, and data layers to produce a single deduplicated incident object with signal lineage, prioritized root-cause hints, and routing hints (oncall/team/customer tier). Deliverables include: a streaming fusion service, an enriched anomaly envelope schema, a deduplication policy engine, and console + webhook alert format changes to consume fused incidents.

Approach summary:
- Ingest anomaly events from existing detectors (usage spike, cost drift, latency SLO breaches) into a lightweight streaming topic (Kafka topic: telemetry.anomalies.raw).
- Enrichment stage: join events with entity metadata (customer region, capacity tier, model variant, most-recent deployment), service topology (region->cluster->node), and recent correlated signals (past 1h window).
- Correlation/fusion stage: apply temporal and topological grouping rules (time bucketing, locality, similarity on feature vectors) to merge events into candidate incident groups. Use a scoring function combining overlap (shared resource), co-occurrence frequency, magnitude, and customer exposure to compute fusion_score.
- Deduplication & priority policy: evaluate candidate groups against per-customer suppression rules, noise heuristics, and SLA tier to emit either: fused_incident (one alert) or individual alerts (when no strong correlation). Add a dedupe_reason and confidence score in metadata.
- Routing & enrichment: annotate fused incidents with recommended routing target (oncall rotation, account success rep), estimated blast radius, and suggested playbook link.
- Feedback loop: accept manual merges/splits from Console and feed back to model/heuristics for supervised improvement.

Non-goals: replace existing detectors. Do not attempt automated remediation in this iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Produces fused_incident objects that consume same schema used by console incident viewer
Reduce duplicate alerts for simulated multi-metric incidents by >=40% in staging test harness
Retain >=95% recall for high-severity incidents (SLA breaches) compared to raw alerts
Expose dedupe_reason, fusion_score, and lineage (list of original alert ids) in emitted object
Console UI shows fused incident with expandable child alerts and allows manual split/merge
Audit log created for every automated merge/split and user-driven action
tasks: Design enriched anomaly envelope schema and backward-compatible consumers
Create telemetry.anomalies.raw Kafka topic and consumer lambda for enrichment
Implement correlation engine (beam/kstream) with time-windowing and topology join
Build policy engine for deduplication rules and per-tenant suppressions
Instrument metrics: emitted_fused_incidents, dedupe_ratio, false_merge_rate, processing_latency
Add console changes: incident viewer grouping and user controls (split/merge)
Create runbook and monitoring dashboards; add automated tests and staging harness
Coordinate with alerts team for webhook format change and pager rules
design_notes:
Core design choice: simple deterministic rules + feature-scoring for v1 to keep behavior explainable and revertible. We will compute a small feature vector per raw alert (resource_id, region, metric_family, magnitude_zscore, tenant_tier, time_bucket) and use a linear scoring model for fusion_score. If confidence < 0.5, avoid automated merge and tag for human review.

State management: use compacted KTables to track active incidents (TTL 72h) and map incoming alerts to active incident windows. Avoid long-lived state to limit memory.

Edge cases: noisy customers generating many small alerts will be rate-limited via per-tenant suppression buckets. Cross-region correlated incidents need special handling: allow cross-region fusion only when a shared upstream dependency is identified in topology metadata.

Privacy: lineage stores only alert ids and metadata used for triage (no raw prompt or customer content).
data_backfill_plan: Backfill raw alerts from the last 90 days into telemetry.anomalies.raw in staging to validate fusion heuristics and compute baseline dedupe_ratio. Create comparison reports (pre/post) using a Jupyter notebook in analytics. Backfill will run partition-parallel using existing ingestion tooling and will be throttled to avoid overload.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy enrichment consumer in staging; validate schema and latency; 2) Enable correlation engine in staging with detection-only mode (emit metrics but do not suppress alerts); 3) Run A/B test on 10% of orgs in production where fused incidents are created but not suppressing raw alerts; 4) Enable suppression for P2/P3 alerts only for 20% sample; 5) Full rollout with monitoring thresholds and ops playbook.

Canary metrics: processing_latency < 2s per alert, dedupe_ratio trending downward, false_merge_rate < 3% in canary sample.
monitoring_and_slas: SLO: correlation engine 99.9% availability. Alert processing 99% under 5 seconds. Export metrics to prometheus: fusion_processing_errors, fused_incident_emitted_total, dedupe_ratio. Add anomaly detection on these internal metrics and a self-monitoring pager.
comments: Priya Patel (PM): Please ensure that tiered suppression can be configured per-customer via the existing customer-config service.
Diego Ramirez (SRE): We need a failure mode where if the fusion service is down, raw alerts pass through unchanged — add a feature flag and fallback route.
Ellen Zhou (Design): Console needs a clear affordance for 'why was this merged' — include dedupe_reason and a one-line human-friendly summary
updates: 2025-11-12: Kickoff meeting held. Agreed to start with deterministic scoring with supervised tuning after 2 weeks of staging data.
2025-11-14: Schema v1 drafted and approved by Console and Alerts teams. PR #2798 opened for schema changes.
2025-11-16: Enrichment consumer implemented; reading from telemetry.anomalies.raw in staging. Initial join with customer metadata added. Processing latency 180ms median in staging.

2025-11-18: Correlation engine prototype running in detection-only mode on 10% staging traffic. Observed candidate fusion events; initial dedupe_ratio 0.47 on synthetic incident test harness. Feedback: increase time-window from 5m -> 10m for long-tail correlated signals.
next_steps: Tune scoring weights and retrain thresholds using 90-day backfill
Implement feature-flagged suppression path and test canary on low-tier customers
Add manual split/merge endpoints and wire into console UI for triage feedback
Write integration tests for failure-mode fallback and schema compatibility
